newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Nam Fong ends debut with modest gains.
newsitem.headline: Nam Fong ends debut with modest gains.

text.p: Shares of China property group Nam Fong International Holdings Ltd ended their trading debut on Monday at HK$3.675 per share, up HK$0.795 or 27.60 percent from the issue price of HK$2.88.
Nam Fong shares hit a high of HK$4.075 in the morning after debuting at HK$3.80. They fell as low as HK$3.55 per share.
Volume was 169.54 million shares worth HK$635.85 million.
"It performed satisfactorily," said Kinson Au, senior analyst at PW Asia Brokerage. "The surge in price was in line with expectations due to its strong subscription level."
Nam Fong offered 340 million new shares -- 272 million to private and institutional investors and 68 million to the public. The initial public offering was 165.6 times subscribed.
"I think the shares were fully valued at above the HK$4.00 level in view of about a 30 to 40 percent discount (of the issue price) to NAV (net asset value)," Au said.
Analysts said they expected the shares to consolidate, with demand for red-chip stocks giving support in the longer run.

They said Hong Kong-based companies with strong focus on China, especially those with ties with Chinese authorities, were increasingly favoured by investors who were eager to tap into the mainland's economic growth.
Nam Fong holds 10 development and two investment properties in China's southern Guangdong province as well as the rights to manage and lease two additional properties.
